databaselibrarylab

A fulldome work is made up of two elements: the visual and the audio.

1 The visual

The visual is usually in the format of a domemaster, which has the dimensions of 1:1. The circle is what gets projected on the dome.

The domemaster can be a rendered video file or a realtime image. It can be two-dimensional or, more often, three-dimensional using 360 camera projection to construct the image.

deeper

Frame sizes run 720, 1024, 1536, 2048, 3200, 3600 or 4096 px a side, as numbered PNG or TARGA with RLE or as JPEG at the highest quality, 8, 10 or 12 bits a colour, at 30 or 60 fps. The Satosphère takes 4096 × 4096 at 60 fps, equidistant fisheye, 210° of field of view on a screen 360° × 210°, and it previews a master at domeport.sat.qc.ca.

A file plays the numbered frames or the movie; a live render sends each frame out as NDI over the network, or as SDI and HDMI on a cable.

Renders come out of Blender, C4D or After Effects, by fisheye, cubemap or a dome camera; TouchDesigner, Processing, vvvv, Unreal, Unity and Ossia Score render in realtime. Resolume and VDMX cut dome clips at a square resolution, with FulldomeVJ, OKVJ and Nest Drop built for it. Festoon and Amateras preview a master on a flat screen or in a headset.

In some cases, the camera can capture fisheye directly.

2 Covering the dome

Domes can have different visual specifications, but in general a combination of projectors cover the surface of the dome. This is done using software like NEST, 7thSense, domeprojection.com or MadMapper, or the warp and blend built into the projectors themselves. Historically it was done with a fisheye lens on one projector, or with a spherical mirror standing on the floor of the dome.

Each projector covers a piece of the dome. The piece is bent to fit the curve so that, once projected, it looks the way it did in the file. Where two pieces meet, they overlap and blend, and the seam reads as one picture.

deeper

No projector covers a hemisphere on its own. A 6 m dome takes three laser projectors at 2.2k or 4k dome resolution and an 18 m dome takes eight at 4.8k, with the blend calibrated in minutes; the Satosphère's 18 m screen takes eight (NEST, SAT).

The mesh that bends each patch is built once for the room — where each projector stands, the radius of the dome, the throw of each lens — and the GPU applies it to every frame.

Paul Bourke built the spherical mirror rig in 2003, and it is still the cheapest way to put one projector on a dome: the projector sits beside the mirror, the mirror spreads the picture over the screen. See paulbourke.net/dome.

3 The audio

The audio is routed through channels to the dome speakers, which often support spatialized audio. Spatial audio means that the channels, rather than routing in stereo to left and right, are routed to surround the audience.

It is possible to have sound move around the room, or to break sound into its parts and have them come from different directions.

There are various algorithms to make this happen that are embedded in tools.

deeper

Multichannel spatialisation writes one channel per speaker: eight, sixteen, or the room's own count. A source becomes gains across the speakers nearest it — vector base amplitude, which SpatGRIS calls DOME; matrix base amplitude, its CUBE, suits rings, halls and theatres; HYBRID sits between the two.

Ambisonics carries the mix instead as spherical harmonics, and the room decodes it to whatever speakers it has — ICST Ambisonics or Spat5 in Max, Envelop for Live. Other tools: Reaper, Nuendo and Pro Tools for the mix; SATIE in SuperCollider; Spat Revolution, Dolby Atmos Production Suite, XP4L. SpatGRIS itself is free, from GRIS at the Université de Montréal, and writes 256 channels in and 256 out.

The Satosphère is 93 loudspeakers and 5 subwoofers over six height levels, and the SpatGRIS setup that ships for it is named Dome93(32-32-16-8-1)Subs 5 Satosphere.

4 Sound with image

Sound and visual can be combined towards immersive effect by controlling the placement of objects in a space and sounds in a space with the same values. This can be directional — one responding to the other — or from a third party.

5 Azimuth and elevation

The dome is imagined with two values: azimuth and elevation. Those two values put a point in X, Y and Z space, and the flat picture needs only x and y.

deeper

Elevation, azimuth and a unit vector are three ways to say one direction. The radius carries the angle from the zenith, so equal steps out from the centre are equal steps down from the top, and 45° sits at half the radius. Mappings that carry solid angle instead — equal area, stereographic, orthographic — trade the even spacing of angle for something else, and Paul Bourke's pages collect them at paulbourke.net/dome.

A 210° dome reaches past the horizon, so its frame carries a margin below the rim: the Satosphère's screen is 360° × 210° and its fisheye field of view matches.

6 Glossary

ambisonics. A mix carried as spherical harmonics rather than a channel per speaker; the room decodes it to the speakers it has.

azimuth. The angle around the dome, 0° at the front and 90° to the right of a viewer at the centre.

channel order. Which speaker each of the file's channels, and each of the interface's outputs, answers to.

ControlGRIS. A plugin that sends source positions and trajectories to SpatGRIS over OSC, driven from a DAW.

CUBE. SpatGRIS's panning for rings, halls and theatres: matrix base amplitude.

cubemap. Six square images, one per direction, that a 360 camera records and a renderer treats as a cube.

DOME. SpatGRIS's panning for speaker domes. Vector base amplitude gives a source gains across the speakers nearest it.

domemaster. The square file holding the hemisphere: the picture fills the circle inscribed in it, black fills the rest.

edge blend. Two projectors' patches overlap at their seam; the blend fades one into the other.

elevation. The angle above the horizon, 0° at the rim of the frame and 90° at the zenith.

equidistant azimuthal. The domemaster's projection. Distance from the centre is the angle from the zenith, so the rings of latitude sit evenly spaced.

fisheye. A lens, or a projection that imitates one, holding a very wide view in a circle.

HYBRID. DOME's panning with CUBE's behaviour, for setups between the two.

interface. The box that turns the software's channels into analogue, MADI or Dante outputs, one per speaker.

NDI. Picture over the network as a stream, rather than a file on disk.

OSC. Open Sound Control: positions, trajectories and cues sent as messages over the network.

SDI. A broadcast coax cable carrying an uncompressed picture between machines.

SpatGRIS. Spatialisation software from GRIS and SAT. It reads source positions over OSC, decodes them onto the speaker setup you draw in it, and writes one output channel per speaker, 256 in and 256 out.

speaker ring. The speakers at one elevation around the dome; a room adds further rings above it.

STEREO. A two-channel mixdown of the spatial mix.

warp. The mesh that bends each projector's patch onto the part of the dome its projector sees.

Sources: SAT, Création Fulldome — Fondamentaux Technique, 2026 · sat.qc.ca · nestimmersion.ca · paulbourke.net/dome · IMERSA and AFDI, Dome Master Specifications, 2019 · GRIS-UdeM/SpatGRIS.
